newsitem.title: FRANCE: Poll shows support returning for France's Chirac.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows support returning for France's Chirac.

text.p: A second opinion poll this week showed public support for conservative French President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe continuing to recover slowly from a low point at the end of last year.

The Louis Harris poll for Valeurs Actuelles magazine, released on Thursday, said 35 percent had a good opinion of Chirac's performance, up three points in a month, while 55 percent were negative, down five points.

The poll, taken on February 7 and 8 with a standard sample of 1,001 adults, showed 29 percent had a good opinion of Juppe's performance, also up three points from January, while 63 percent were negative, down four points.

The survey showed a slight decline in economic pessimism in France. Sixty percent of those questioned said the economic and social situation was getting worse, 10 percent thought it was improving and 30 percent said it was unchanged.

The number of optimists rose by four points and the number of pessimists was down two points. But 77 percent of respondents said they felt a greater risk of being unemployed than a year ago, while only 14 percent thought the risk had declined.
An IFOP institute poll released on Wednesday, asking a slightly different question, showed a more spectacular rise in Juppe's approval rating.
It found 40 percent of voters had confidence in the centre-right prime minister, up from 31 percent last December.
Chirac's standing was also up at 47 percent from 44, according to the poll of 950 voters for the weekly L'Express.
